summary: The ML platform landscape in 2026 has consolidated around a handful of cloud-native and multi-cloud offerings, with the global MLOps market reaching $4.39B and projected to grow at 45.8% CAGR through 2034. Azure ML, AWS SageMaker, and Databricks Mosaic AI lead enterprise adoption, while specialized platforms like DataRobot and H2O.ai serve domain-specific needs. You need a full ML platform when managing complex model lifecycles, governance, multi-team collaboration, or LLM/agent pipelines at scale — if you only need inference, a model API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) is far simpler and cheaper.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go compute; free tier for experimentation; enterprise agreements available. Compute costs dominate (e.g., NC-series GPU VMs from ~$0.90/hr to $30+/hr).
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-heavy enterprises needing mature MLOps, strong governance, and deep Azure ecosystem integration (Teams, Fabric, Purview).

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use compute and storage. ml.t3.medium instances from ~$0.05/hr; GPU instances (ml.p4d.24xlarge) up to ~$32/hr. Inference endpoints billed per instance-hour. No platform fee beyond AWS usage.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native teams needing breadth of ML tooling, infrastructure control, and tight integration with S3, Glue, Redshift, and other AWS services.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
capabilities: MLflow 3.x experiment tracking and model registry
AI gateway for LLM routing and governance
platforms.pricing: DBU (Databricks Unit) consumption model. Jobs compute from ~$0.07/DBU; ML compute tier ~$0.22/DBU. Model serving charged per token or per instance-hour. Significant discounts via annual commits.
platforms.best_for: Data-centric organizations running unified analytics and ML on a lakehouse, especially those needing multi-cloud flexibility and strong data governance alongside AI.

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
capabilities: AutoML for structured, image, text, and video data
Custom model training with distributed compute
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go. Training node hours vary by accelerator (TPU v4 pods, A100s). Prediction charged per compute hour or per 1K characters for managed models. Gemini API calls priced per token.
platforms.best_for: GCP-native teams and organizations with heavy generative AI and data analytics workloads, especially those leveraging BigQuery, Looker, or Google's foundation models.

platforms.name: Databricks MLflow (standalone / open-source)
capabilities: Model registry with versioning and stage transitions
Integration with PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, HuggingFace, LangChain
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host. Managed via Databricks platform (see Databricks pricing). No standalone SaaS pricing.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting framework-agnostic, open-source experiment tracking and model registry without vendor lock-in, often used as the glue layer in custom MLOps stacks.

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Free and open-source. Infrastructure costs only (Kubernetes cluster, GPUs). Managed distributions available via Arrikto, Canonical, or cloud marketplaces.
platforms.best_for: Organizations with strong DevOps/platform engineering teams that need Kubernetes-native ML orchestration with full control and no vendor lock-in.

platforms.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
capabilities: Integration with PyTorch, TensorFlow, HuggingFace, LightGBM, and more
platforms.pricing: Free tier (personal use, 100GB storage). Team plan ~$50/user/month. Enterprise pricing custom. Compute not included — connects to user's own infra.
platforms.best_for: Research teams, ML engineers, and enterprises needing best-in-class experiment tracking, visualization, and model evaluation across any training infrastructure.

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.cloud: Multi-cloud SaaS or private cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, on-prem)
capabilities: Automated ML (AutoML) for tabular, text, and time-series
platforms.pricing: Subscription-based, enterprise pricing only. Typically $50K–$250K+/year depending on usage tier and deployment model. No public self-serve pricing.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises and data science teams that need rapid AutoML, strong model governance, and business-user accessibility without deep ML engineering overhead.

platforms.name: Domino Data Lab
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription only. Pricing based on compute and seats; typically $100K+/year for enterprise contracts. Private cloud deployment available.
platforms.best_for: Large enterprises in regulated industries (finance, pharma, healthcare) needing strong reproducibility, audit trails, and compliance alongside full ML lifecycle management.

platforms.name: H2O.ai
capabilities: H2O AutoML for automated model building
Driverless AI for automated feature engineering
H2O MLOps for deployment and monitoring
LLM fine-tuning and evaluation (H2O LLM Studio)
platforms.pricing: H2O-3 is open-source and free. Driverless AI and H2O Enterprise AI Cloud are subscription-based (contact sales; typically $40K–$200K+/year). H2O LLM Studio is open-source.
platforms.best_for: Organizations needing powerful AutoML, explainability, and flexible deployment across cloud or on-prem, particularly in financial services, insurance, and healthcare.

platforms.name: Dataiku
platforms.cloud: Multi-cloud SaaS or on-prem (AWS, Azure, GCP)
capabilities: Visual and code-based ML pipeline builder
Model deployment to cloud or on-prem endpoints
LLM plugin integrations and prompt studios
Collaboration tools for data scientists and analysts
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription. Pricing not public; typically $50K–$300K+/year based on users and compute. Free Community Edition available for individuals.
platforms.best_for: Cross-functional data teams (analysts, scientists, engineers) in large enterprises that need a collaborative, low-code/high-code hybrid platform with strong governance.

platforms.name: Modal
capabilities: Serverless GPU compute for training and inference
Web endpoint deployment for model APIs
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second compute. GPU pricing from ~$0.74/hr (A10G) to ~$4.13/hr (A100 80GB). Generous free tier ($30 credit/month). No infrastructure management fees.
platforms.best_for: ML engineers and startups wanting serverless, code-first GPU infrastructure for fine-tuning, batch inference, and model APIs without managing Kubernetes or cloud VMs.

notable_opus_additions: Google Vertex AI (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
